question.text: An organization having which of the following characteristics pose a VALID social objective per Ch 1.4.2?

answer.text: An enterprise whose primary bottom line is maximising shareholder profit and redistributing it among its board/staff
An organisation created to serve social good, with a social mission, creating social value through social change and building social capital
An organisation focused solely on financial returns but incidentally benefiting society
A for-profit entity whose profit is distributed as dividend to all shareholders

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 1.4.2, a Social Objective denotes the entity is created / incorporated to serve a social good, has a social mission, creates social value through social change, builds social capital and has a social bottom line. Profit-redistribution-to-stakeholders disqualifies social-objective status. **The Trap:** Options A, C and D all center profit/dividend — opposite of social-objective. Option B is the correct chapter definition. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to Ch 4 (Logic Model), Ch 6 (Frameworks). SIAs probe the 'objects clause' of the charter to validate primacy of social objective — not a mission-statement in the brochure. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Compare the SE's objects clause verbatim with its latest Annual Report mission statement. Divergence between legal and operational statements is a governance red flag. Document this comparison in your working papers.
